methodology_and_limits: All samples retained: no filtering, trimming, selection, or winsorization. Changes are ON/OFF minus one; negative is faster.
CPU and allocations are current-region-thread ThreadMXBean counters. Wall time is System.nanoTime. Two TCP clients remain connected; region benchmark phases execute sequentially.
Pooled sample medians are descriptive. Per-process and per-process-per-region distributions are also retained; rounds and regions within one JVM are not independent process replicates.
Final OFF and ON share safety fixes and common memory-version maintenance. Original reference is one separate older-artifact process and is never merged into OFF.
Complete Brain.tick uses real villagers and sensors with synthetic 96-task or 4-task graphs, not an unchanged vanilla villager brain. Churn toggles memory presence every tick.
Block entity timings invoke actual LevelChunk ticker wrappers. Bulk operation means 64 wrappers. The outer Level scheduler and midTickTasks are excluded; repeated ticks share server game time.
Bulk active work counts wrapper invocations. Natural-tick output/progress, wakeup and redstone transfer are separately asserted in functional runs; counts alone do not prove output equivalence.
Subset timings do not establish whole-server throughput, MSPT or TPS improvement. No claim covers all plugins/redstone/gameplay patterns.

Async fallback is conservative: removed unsafe block states may persist in section palettes. Correct owner completion and static-corridor asynchronous paths are asserted; asynchronous nonblocking throughput is not measured.
Final fresh and restart checks passed in all four final-process arms. Baseline reference skips new-API functional checks.
Bulk active states are non-sleeping workloads, not full production throughput: crafter countdown, incomplete campfire cooking, open shulker, and unlocked hopper empty queries.
